summary: Add a contributor-only BIOS guest persistence acceptance adapter for the current ISO. API impact: none; it uses the installed host's existing libvirt and an explicitly selected private guest fixture, without adding or changing any Nex Controller, Core, or client contract. The adapter verifies a standalone qcow2 fixture and an explicit guest host key, never formats an image container, and retains private artifacts if lifecycle release fails.

guide.reason: This is private contributor QA for an already installed disposable host; it adds no operator workflow or product behavior.

api.reason: The adapter invokes local libvirt and private SSH only; it introduces no Nex API operation or changed contract.

roadmap.reason: The helper verifies a bounded BIOS fixture without completing the wider production milestone.

state.reason: The independently converted guest disk, SSH key copy, domain definition and result are private disposable-lab artifacts. Successful release undefines the stopped guest; failures retain the exact fixture for diagnosis. No product durable state is added.

verification.method: Focused 12-test suite passed; corrected per-unit baseline refused the unhealthy fifth-ISO installation. On the independently audited seventh ISO, actual clean BIOS installation/disk-only boot and required services passed. After explicit disposable NAT preparation, a newly converted standalone BIOS guest wrote/fsynced data and verified its checksum across guest and host reboots with distinct boot identities. It was shut down/undefined and its disk retained. Independent live-host review accepted the receipt, current services/private directories, binary/source pins and zero domains. Local desktop/mobile browser review passed. Earlier failed evidence remains retained; UEFI, physical hardware and production certification are not claimed. Integration helpers remain outside the shipped source-archive allowlist.
